subject: Order form: third-party IP carveout & evidence custody proposal
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@tripleplay.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procure@tripleplay.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: TriplePlay Order Form - proposed indemnity carveout for third-party model IP claims

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft order form. We reviewed the indemnity section and attached a redline (TriplePlay_Redlines_20260301.docx) that includes a carveout we need for third-party model IP claims. In short: because we (TriplePlay) will be using a mix of open models, third-party licensed models, and our own fine-tunes, we are asking that Redwood limit indemnity for "third-party IP claims" to scenarios where Redwood (a) controlled the model training/fine-tune that produced the infringing output, or (b) provided the specific model artifact under Redwood's redistribution/license.

We also have a practical evidence request: if a claim is raised, TriplePlay needs the ability to preserve and receive the output sample, prompt context, and any model hash/identifier. We propose that the contract require Redwood to cooperate and, where Redwood materially controls the model, to take the lead on defense. Where TriplePlay controlled prompts/fine-tunes, we expect any defense/reimbursement obligation to be capped and conditioned on us providing the preservation packet.

We're aiming to keep this close to market but cannot accept a broad unconditional indemnity for third-party model IP where we are using customer or third-party-supplied artifacts. Can we set a call for today to walk through the redline?

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Head of Procurement
TriplePlay AI

Attachment: TriplePlay_Redlines_20260301.docx (redline of Order Form indemnity + evidence section)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@tripleplay.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-03-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TriplePlay Order Form - proposed indemnity carveout for third-party model IP claims

Hi Elena — thanks for sending the redline and the clear ask. Appreciate the signal on evidence custody; that's helpful context.

Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Jordan (solutions) so we can align quickly. Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly to review and propose narrow language that protects both parties (Redwood will own defense where we provided or fully managed a model; TriplePlay would retain responsibility for customer-managed/fine-tune cases).
- Jordan and I to confirm operational feasibility for evidence collection (model hashes, output samples, prompt capture).
- 30-min sync today at 3pm PT to go line-by-line if that works for you — happy to adjust.

Kimberly/Jordan: high level — TriplePlay is asking us to carve our indemnity for third-party IP claims so it only applies when Redwood had control over the model artifact or training. They also want a contractual preservation packet requirement before we take on any reimbursement. Can you advise on whether we can offer: (1) a defend obligation when Redwood is the model provider; (2) a limited reimbursement obligation (cap + conditional) when customer prompts/fine-tunes are implicated; (3) a required evidence-preservation step prior to payment or indemnity triggers?

Elena — we can share suggested language ahead of the call; I attached a short summary we use internally.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Indemnity_Suggested_Language_20260301.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@tripleplay.ai>, procure@tripleplay.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T13:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TriplePlay Order Form - proposed indemnity carveout for third-party model IP claims — legal analysis and proposed compromise

Lauren/Jordan/Elena — I reviewed TriplePlay's redline. High level takeaways and suggested path:

1) Core principle: Redwood will defend/reimburse for third-party IP claims only when the claim arises from a model artifact that Redwood supplied or where Redwood controlled the training/fine-tune process ("Redwood‑Controlled Model"). This protects us for SaaS-hosted, Redwood-curated models.

2) Customer-controlled artifacts: where the customer supplies prompts, datasets, or a customer-managed fine-tune that materially contributed to the infringing output, Redwood's obligation will be limited to a reimbursement cap (e.g., up to $250k) and conditioned on TriplePlay providing the required preservation packet (see below). We should also require that TriplePlay promptly notify Redwood and not materially alter evidence.

3) Evidence preservation packet: to avoid spurious claims, require the following as a precondition to indemnity/reimbursement: (a) sample output, (b) full prompt/context metadata (time, user id, request id), (c) model identifier (hash or canonical name and version), (d) any customer-supplied datasets/fine-tune manifest. If Redwood is unable to validate the model identifier or where evidence is incomplete, Redwood may deny or limit coverage.

4) Defense control: Redwood will seek control of defense (reasonable counsel selection and settlement authority) for Redwood‑Controlled Model claims. For customer-controlled scenarios, reimbursement will be subject to customer cooperation and Redwood's approval of counsel to manage proportionality.

5) Operational notes: Jordan — we need a short SOP for evidence capture and a retention window we can commit to (suggest 90 days for streaming captures unless customer opts-in to extended retention).

6) Draft language: (i) define "Redwood‑Controlled Model"; (ii) carve out third-party models provided by the customer; (iii) add explicit preservation packet as condition precedent; (iv) reimbursement cap and insurance carve for customer-managed scenarios. I attached a redline with proposed text and fallback positions.

Proposed ask of TriplePlay on the call: agree to the preservation process and to a mutually acceptable reimbursement cap. If they're insistent on an unconditional broad indemnity, we should propose an insurance-offset and a materiality threshold (e.g., claims > $X).

Happy to talk through line-by-line at 3pm PT.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Indemnity_Suggested_Language_20260301.pdf (detailed redline and fallback options)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@tripleplay.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-03-01T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TriplePlay Order Form - proposed indemnity carveout for third-party model IP claims — next steps

Elena — thanks for the redline and for joining the call. Quick recap and proposed mutual action plan so we have it in writing before legal redlines: 

1) Principle: Redwood will accept defend/reimburse obligations for third‑party IP claims only when the claim arises from a Redwood‑Controlled Model (Redwood-supplied model artifact or training).

2) Customer-managed artifacts: for claims linked to customer-supplied / customer-managed fine-tunes, Redwood will offer a limited reimbursement path (cap $250k) conditioned on TriplePlay providing the preservation packet within 30 days of notice and allowing Redwood to validate model identifiers.

3) Preservation packet: TriplePlay to provide sample output, prompt context (request id and timestamps), model identifier/hash, and any manifest for fine-tunes. Both parties agreed this is a condition precedent to reimbursement/coverage.

4) Evidence retention: Jordan will share a short SOP for how Redwood captures model identifiers in hosted routes and proposed retention window (we suggested 90 days default; TriplePlay requested 180 days as an option).

5) Fallbacks: if evidence is incomplete, Redwood may decline or prorate coverage. For high-severity claims (> $1M), both parties will pursue good‑faith mediation before settlement.

Next steps / owners:
- Kimberly: send final redline with defined term "Redwood‑Controlled Model" and the conditional reimbursement language (by EOD 3/2).
- Jordan: draft SOP and retention options (by 3/3).
- Lauren: update HubSpot (TP-2026-0091) with agreed summary and schedule follow-up with procurement to finalize order form (Docs/DocuSign link to follow).

If this captures the outcome for TriplePlay, we'll incorporate the language into the Order Form and route for signatures. Thanks again for the productive conversation.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
